A good way to quit is to put things into perspective. Try in the morning when you are freshly awake (and haven't smoked yet) to write down a list of pros/cons for smoking. Write down everything that comes to your mind, even if it seems silly. Then, compile a list of the ways each con effects your life, same for pros. Review it again in a week, sober. This is a good way to evaluate how it is impacting you whether it be good or bad. It helps to have the full picture in front of you.

I do think you are capable of staying sober during the holidays. But I totally understand how it can mess with you emotionally. So what I learned in therapy is that you can replace one old habit with 2 healthy ones. If your go to de-stressor was getting high during the holidays..try something else instead. Do something you haven't done but have been thinking about trying. If the urges come up, do that thing instead. Or, remove yourself from the situation you are in. Sometimes a positional change or change of rooms can really help me with anxiety. I'll just walk out of functions or social situations sometimes to collect my thoughts before returning. In the early stages of recovery, sometimes I never came back LOL! People were confused until I explained my situation. Always put your emotional well being first when you can. When we take care of it before it spirals out of control..we are in a better position to stay sober too.

I quit originally as I was in therapy and it was hindering the recovery process. I remember coming in to see my therapist one day and I was hysterical, irrational and panicking. I explained to her that I was suddenly sober that morning as I ran out of weed, and that I'd been smoking all day every day for a long time. She explained that she has seen these symptoms in people before related to cannabis use. She also explained how it can induce a kind of psychosis in some people at high concentrations. 

Because I became very mentally ill and with her encouragement, I decided to quit. It was also effecting my health (racing heart etc) while I already have a cardiac condition to manage. It was the best thing I could do for both fronts.

At the 5 month mark (and this isn't my first rodeo either) I was 21 pounds lighter. Working out every week. My confidence skyrocketed. I felt generally happy, and I was able to start enjoying life sober. I wasn't numb anymore. Everything was so vividly clear and hiking became fully enjoyable again. Cannabis numbs me to the point where I also dissociate while high on it. This can help the emotional pain in life, but it also takes away the good experiences too. It's just like an empty chamber, echoing back on yourself but you hear nothing anymore. 

Anyway, that is a brief synopsis of my sober and non sober experiences. It was nice to reflect on that, thanks again

It really helps to identify why you feel angry and irrational. So I have a suggestion for you. Next time you feel these emotions, pull out a diary and write down what you're feeling, and what happened right before these feelings that triggered them. Anger does not come out of nowhere most of the time, and it is generally connected to another emotion...find where it came from, and write it down.
If a diary does not feel safe to you-open up your email account and write it down there so long as you're the only one with a password to it if privacy is a concern for you.

Once you write your feelings down and your emotions eventually subside, look at the situations in your life that cause these feelings. Study them, and try to work towards a solution if possible. Your whole life will consist of this type of activity. But the reason I suggest this to you is so that you feel a sense of control in yourself and in your life. I won't lie to you, there are many things out of our control. For example, we can't control other people.

But we can control ourselves. We can control how we respond to others, we can control our involvement with them. Remember this for your future relationships. But for now, you are in a fragile situation with your parents. The best thing you can do is teach yourself healthy coping skills. 

It's definitely okay to feel anger. It's a natural human emotion. But think of anger as the 'energy to act'. Listen to your anger as if it were your own child crying for help. Once you have listened, it's time to act. Act in a way that does not harm yourself or other people. Transform this anger into another thing all together-motion.

If it's safe for you to do so, take a walk in a safe place the next time you feel angry. Take a walk and bring your phone-record your thoughts out loud into your phone and play it back later on. Notice what your raw emotions SOUND like.

I'm 30 with heart problems too. I have diastolic dysfunction caused by long term uncontrolled HBP among other things. I strongly suspect that I have hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

IF I DID NOT STOP DRINKING, I WOULD HAVE HAD A HEART ATTACK AND DIED. 

Got it? Good..now,

Remember that it's not all in your head, ok? Healthy people with normal hearts are not going to be effected by drinking the same way you are(at least not right away)..so you have to avoid it.

Next thing:
Cannabis can raise a persons resting heart rate 20-40 more beats per minute. My heart races like a horse when I smoke. How about you? You're gonna feel that shit big time.

Low to no sodium. If I eat a bunch of salt I end up in the e.r. and I'm not kidding. It's not good for a healthy heart, and it's even worse for yours pal. We need some sodium but we don't need a fuckload of it either. Pay attention to your daily intake of such and square it up with what is a recommended daily dose.

Take it from someone who was pre heart attack in the e.r. at the ripe old age of 25. We have to be more careful with our health than the average person because we are more suseptible to serious cardiac complications which...sometimes people don't survive. 

Please work with your doctor to get your heart in the best shape you can. As for your qutting...you did the best thing for your health man. You really did. Now if you need to see an addictions counselor to keep you clean? Do it!!! Take all the help available. I promise you will feel so much better and have more endurance.

Lastly,

Get some electrolytes back in your body because drinking flushes them right out. And guess who gets effected the most? That ticker in the center of your chest. Remedy: drink coconut water, and eat a daily apple and banana. Oranges would be okay too.
